data.why: The tool takes no file uploads; all inputs (population size, noise exposure distribution, baseline rates) are typed directly into form fields with sensible pre-filled defaults.

goals: Estimate the number of attributable cases per year of ischemic heart disease, stroke, heart failure, and type 2 diabetes from road traffic noise exposure in a defined population
Estimate attributable cardiovascular deaths and years of life lost (YLL) from chronic noise exposure
Quantify high annoyance and high sleep disturbance prevalence using WHO exposure-response functions
Compute total Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) combining YLD and YLL across all selected health outcomes
Run sensitivity analyses across counterfactual noise levels, disability weight presets, and alternative relative-risk estimates for ischemic heart disease
Export a CSV report of attributable cases, rates, PAFs, and DALYs for further analysis or documentation

review.summary: The tree captures NoiseQ+'s purpose and its 6-step burden-estimation workflow well. It also rightly records that the sensitivity analyses can only be read, not run with chosen values, despite the README's wording. Before filing it needs a few fixes: one screen cited for threshold-mode entry actually shows Results, Lden is mislabelled as 'daytime-weighted', and the Methods evidence/limitations task and a Methods feature are missing.
